To find the order $\beta$ of the Rényi entropy $H_\beta(X)$ to which Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information $I_\alpha(X; Y)$ converges as $\mathsf{snr} \to \infty$, we recall the definition of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information:
$$I_\alpha(X; Y) = \min_{Q_Y} D_\alpha(P_{XY} \| P_X \otimes Q_Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha-1} \log \int \left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy$$

For the additive Gaussian channel $Y = \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} X + Z$ with $Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, the transition density is:
$$p(y|x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$
so that
$$p(y|x)^\alpha = (2\pi)^{-\alpha/2} \exp\left( -\frac{\alpha(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$

As $\mathsf{snr} \to \infty$, the points $\sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x$ become well-separated. In the neighborhood of each $y \approx \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x$, the sum $\sum_{x'} P(x') p(y|x')^\alpha$ is dominated by the single term $x' = x$. Taking the $1/\alpha$ power gives:
$$\left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} \approx \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$

Integrating over $y \in \mathbb{R}$, each Gaussian component integrates to $1$, yielding:
$$\lim_{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} \int \left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy = \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Thus,
$$\lim_{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} I_\alpha(X; Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha-1} \log \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha} = \frac{1}{1 - 1/\alpha} \log \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Comparing this with the definition of the Rényi entropy of order $\beta$,
$$H_\beta(X) = \frac{1}{1-\beta} \log \sum_x P(x)^\beta$$
we identify $\beta = \frac{1}{\alpha}$.

ANSWER: 1/\alpha
